correctness.rationale: A proper common prefix/suffix cannot contain both ones; a zero-only border has maximum min(a,c), while a one-one border must have length a+c+1 and exists exactly when b>=max(a,c). Disjoint integer-lattice counts yield A_n(t)+D_n(t) and the rational bivariate series. Their uniform piecewise n f(t/n)/2+O(1) count gives the local limit. Exact rational integration yields E[Z]=7/27, E[Z^2]=5/54, variance=37/1458. KMP checked 121485 words of lengths 2..90, bivariate coefficient extraction to zero-degree 35, normalizations and maxima to n=2000. Computations are corroboration, not proof.

value.rationale: The longest border is a natural overlap/least-period statistic relevant to synchronization and string algorithms. Exact border-length counts and the rational bivariate series cover the entire infinite fixed-weight-two family, and the uniform local law shows a macroscopic phase transition at border fraction 1/3 with endpoint 2/3. Competing zero-only and one-marker overlap mechanisms first coexist at Hamming weight two; the explicit conditional law distinguishes this sparse regime from the established O(1) unrestricted law. This is more than isolated numerical checks or a reparameterization; it solves a complete natural stochastic enumeration problem.
